title: Decoding da Vinci | Full Documentary | NOVA | PBS
speaker: NOVA PBS Official
zh: 【NOVA PBS Official】解碼達文西|完整紀錄片 |新星|公共廣播公司（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：李奧納多‧達文西。

cues.text: Legendary artist.
cues.en: Legendary artist.
cues.zh: 傳奇藝術家。

cues.text: VINCENT DELIEUVIN: His genius is universal.
cues.en: VINCENT DELIEUVIN: His genius is universal.
cues.zh: VINCENT DELIEUVIN：他的天才是普遍的。

cues.text: It speaks to everybody.
cues.en: It speaks to everybody.
cues.zh: 它對每個人都有影響。

cues.text: NARRATOR: He was also a scientist and inventor.
cues.en: NARRATOR: He was also a scientist and inventor.
cues.zh: 旁白：他也是一位科學家和發明家。

cues.text: KARLY BAST: There was a reason for every decision and every line.
cues.en: KARLY BAST: There was a reason for every decision and every line.
cues.zh: KARLY BAST：每一個決定和每一條臺詞都是有原因的。

cues.text: NARRATOR: How did he create the most famous painting on Earth?
cues.en: NARRATOR: How did he create the most famous painting on Earth?
cues.zh: 旁白：他是如何創作出地球上最著名的畫作的？

cues.text: FRANCESCA BORGO: You can perceive the beating of the pulse underneath her skin.
cues.en: FRANCESCA BORGO: You can perceive the beating of the pulse underneath her skin.
cues.zh: 弗朗西斯卡·博爾戈：你可以感覺到她皮膚下的脈搏跳動。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: The answers have been as elusive as her smile.
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: The answers have been as elusive as her smile.
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：答案就像她的微笑一樣難以捉摸。

cues.text: Leonardo embraced mystery.
cues.en: Leonardo embraced mystery.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多擁抱神秘。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Now researchers are peeling away the layers.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Now researchers are peeling away the layers.
cues.zh: 旁白：現在研究人員正在剝去這些層。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Thanks to a new kind of scientific investigation, we are really able to get inside the painting.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Thanks to a new kind of scientific investigation, we are really able to get inside the painting.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：多虧了一種新的科學研究，我們才真正能夠進入這幅畫的內部。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Can science unlock her secrets?
cues.en: NARRATOR: Can science unlock her secrets?
cues.zh: 旁白：科學能解開她的秘密嗎？

cues.text: MARGARET LIVINGSTONE: She seems like she's alive, because she looks different depending on where you're looking.
cues.en: MARGARET LIVINGSTONE: She seems like she's alive, because she looks different depending on where you're looking.
cues.zh: 瑪格麗特·利文斯通：她看起來就像還活著，因為根據你看的地方，她看起來會有所不同。

cues.text: NARRATOR: And decipher the genius behind her creator?
cues.en: NARRATOR: And decipher the genius behind her creator?
cues.zh: 旁白：解讀她的創造者背後的天才？

cues.text: "Decoding da Vinci," right now, on "NOVA." ♪
cues.en: "Decoding da Vinci," right now, on "NOVA." ♪
cues.zh: “解碼達文西”，現在在“NOVA”節目中。 ♪

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: In the heart of Paris lies a former royal castle.
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: In the heart of Paris lies a former royal castle.
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：巴黎市中心坐落著一座前皇家城堡。

cues.text: It is now the world's busiest art museum:
cues.en: It is now the world's busiest art museum:
cues.zh: 它現在是世界上最繁忙的藝術博物館：

cues.text: the Louvre.
cues.en: the Louvre.
cues.zh: 盧浮宮。

cues.text: Filled with glorious galleries of antiquities, mummies, and Michelangelos.
cues.en: Filled with glorious galleries of antiquities, mummies, and Michelangelos.
cues.zh: 充滿了輝煌的古董、木乃伊和米開朗基羅畫廊。

cues.text: ♪ But one masterpiece is the biggest draw of all.
cues.en: ♪ But one masterpiece is the biggest draw of all.
cues.zh: ♪ 但一件傑作才是最吸引人的。

cues.text: Today's reigning queen-- the "Mona Lisa," by Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.en: Today's reigning queen-- the "Mona Lisa," by Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.zh: 今天的女王－列奧納多·達·芬奇的《蒙娜麗莎》。

cues.text: WALTER ISAACSON: The "Mona Lisa" has become some grand thing in our imagination.
cues.en: WALTER ISAACSON: The "Mona Lisa" has become some grand thing in our imagination.
cues.zh: 華特‧艾薩克森：《蒙娜麗莎》已經成為我們想像中的宏偉之物。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Each time you see the "Mona Lisa," you have a different feeling
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Each time you see the "Mona Lisa," you have a different feeling
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：每次看《蒙娜麗莎》都有不同的感受

cues.text: about what she has in mind.
cues.en: about what she has in mind.
cues.zh: 關於她的想法。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Every year, millions visit her, drawn by her beauty
cues.en: NARRATOR: Every year, millions visit her, drawn by her beauty
cues.zh: 旁白：每年都有數百萬人被她的美麗所吸引而拜訪她

cues.text: or, perhaps, her fame.
cues.en: or, perhaps, her fame.
cues.zh: 或者，也許是她的名氣。

cues.text: BORGO: They've clocked the average amount the visitors spend looking at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.en: BORGO: They've clocked the average amount the visitors spend looking at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.zh: 博爾戈：他們統計了遊客觀看《蒙娜麗莎》的平均花費，

cues.text: and that's roughly about 15 seconds.
cues.en: and that's roughly about 15 seconds.
cues.zh: 大約需要 15 秒。

cues.text: You're more focused on getting a good picture for your Instagram feed than actually looking at the painting.
cues.en: You're more focused on getting a good picture for your Instagram feed than actually looking at the painting.
cues.zh: 您更專注於為 Instagram 動態獲取一張好照片，而不是實際觀看這幅畫。

cues.text: NARRATOR: So is the "Mona Lisa" just famous for being famous?
cues.en: NARRATOR: So is the "Mona Lisa" just famous for being famous?
cues.zh: 旁白：那麼《蒙娜麗莎》只是因為出名而出名嗎？

cues.text: More icon than art?
cues.en: More icon than art?
cues.zh: 更多的是圖示而不是藝術？

cues.text: Or does she deserve her place on the Louvre's throne as the most celebrated painting in the world?
cues.en: Or does she deserve her place on the Louvre's throne as the most celebrated painting in the world?
cues.zh: 或者她配得上羅浮宮作為世界上最著名的畫作的寶座？

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: It's not just a portrait of a woman who was living 500 years ago.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: It's not just a portrait of a woman who was living 500 years ago.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：這不僅僅是一幅生活在 500 年前的女性的肖像。

cues.text: It's a demonstration of how painting could show life.
cues.en: It's a demonstration of how painting could show life.
cues.zh: 這是繪畫如何展現生活的示範。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Now researchers are using new techniques to investigate the most famous painting on Earth
cues.en: NARRATOR: Now researchers are using new techniques to investigate the most famous painting on Earth
cues.zh: 旁白：現在研究人員正在使用新技術來研究地球上最著名的畫作

cues.text: like never before.
cues.en: like never before.
cues.zh: 前所未有。

cues.text: ♪ MARTIN KEMP: The smile is crucial.
cues.en: ♪ MARTIN KEMP: The smile is crucial.
cues.zh: ♪ 馬丁坎普：微笑至關重要。

cues.text: It's teasing you, saying, "I know something you don't know."
cues.en: It's teasing you, saying, "I know something you don't know."
cues.zh: 它在戲弄你，說：“我知道一些你不知道的事情。”

cues.text: NARRATOR: Could the "Mona Lisa," with her enigmatic smile,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Could the "Mona Lisa," with her enigmatic smile,
cues.zh: 旁白：帶著神秘微笑的“蒙娜麗莎”，

cues.text: be the key to decoding the man who made her--
cues.en: be the key to decoding the man who made her--
cues.zh: 成為破解創造她的男人的鑰匙——

cues.text: Leonardo da Vinci?
cues.en: Leonardo da Vinci?
cues.zh: 列奧納多·達·芬奇？

cues.text: No doubt he was a brilliant artist, but he was also a groundbreaking scientist.
cues.en: No doubt he was a brilliant artist, but he was also a groundbreaking scientist.
cues.zh: 毫無疑問，他是一位傑出的藝術家，但他也是一位開創性的科學家。

cues.text: He anticipated theories by both Galileo and Newton
cues.en: He anticipated theories by both Galileo and Newton
cues.zh: 他預見了伽利略和牛頓的理論

cues.text: by at least a century.
cues.en: by at least a century.
cues.zh: 至少一個世紀。

cues.text: And dreamed up remarkable inventions that seem to predict our modern age:
cues.en: And dreamed up remarkable inventions that seem to predict our modern age:
cues.zh: 並夢想著一些非凡的發明，這些發明似乎預示著我們的現代時代：

cues.text: armored tanks, flying machines, even something like a self-driving car.
cues.en: armored tanks, flying machines, even something like a self-driving car.
cues.zh: 裝甲坦克、飛行器，甚至自動駕駛汽車之類的東西。

cues.text: But were his scientific explorations a distraction from his painting?
cues.en: But were his scientific explorations a distraction from his painting?
cues.zh: 但他的科學探索會分散他對繪畫的注意力嗎？

cues.text: Or was science the secret to his artistic genius?
cues.en: Or was science the secret to his artistic genius?
cues.zh: 或者科學是他藝術天才的秘密？

cues.text: Was the "Mona Lisa," in fact, Leonardo's greatest invention?
cues.en: Was the "Mona Lisa," in fact, Leonardo's greatest invention?
cues.zh: 《蒙娜麗莎》其實是李奧納多最偉大的發明嗎？

cues.text: ISAACSON: If you want to understand Leonardo da Vinci, you just have to look at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.en: ISAACSON: If you want to understand Leonardo da Vinci, you just have to look at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：如果你想了解達文西，你只需要看看《蒙娜麗莎》

cues.text: because it's all there.
cues.en: because it's all there.
cues.zh: 因為一切都在那裡。

cues.text: It's the culmination of a lifetime spent loving science and art.
cues.en: It's the culmination of a lifetime spent loving science and art.
cues.zh: 這是一生熱愛科學和藝術的頂峰。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: In the back streets of Florence, Italy,
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: In the back streets of Florence, Italy,
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：在義大利佛羅倫斯的後街，

cues.text: Valter Conti and his daughter Elena prepare for their tribute to Leonardo
cues.en: Valter Conti and his daughter Elena prepare for their tribute to Leonardo
cues.zh: 瓦爾特·孔蒂和他的女兒埃琳娜準備向萊昂納多致敬

cues.text: and the "Mona Lisa"...
cues.en: and the "Mona Lisa"...
cues.zh: 還有《蒙娜麗莎》…

cues.text: Human statues handing out Leonardo quotes.
cues.en: Human statues handing out Leonardo quotes.
cues.zh: 人體雕像分發達芬奇名言。

cues.text: It's their way of marking the 500th anniversary
cues.en: It's their way of marking the 500th anniversary
cues.zh: 這是他們紀念 500 週年的方式

cues.text: of Leonardo's death, and just one of many celebrations
cues.en: of Leonardo's death, and just one of many celebrations
cues.zh: 萊昂納多去世，這只是眾多慶祝活動之一

cues.text: that are in the works around the world.
cues.en: that are in the works around the world.
cues.zh: 世界各地都在進行中。

cues.text: From a fine art museum in Beijing to a multimedia extravaganza in Peru...
cues.en: From a fine art museum in Beijing to a multimedia extravaganza in Peru...
cues.zh: 從北京的美術館到秘魯的多媒體盛宴…

cues.text: And a blockbuster exhibition at the Louvre.
cues.en: And a blockbuster exhibition at the Louvre.
cues.zh: 以及在羅浮宮舉辦的一場轟動一時的展覽。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: For the Louvre museum, it's a really important moment.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: For the Louvre museum, it's a really important moment.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：對羅浮宮來說，這是一個非常重要的時刻。

cues.text: Because Louvre is like Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.en: Because Louvre is like Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.zh: 因為羅浮宮就像達文西。

cues.text: We have the third of all his paintings.
cues.en: We have the third of all his paintings.
cues.zh: 我們擁有他所有畫作中的第三幅。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Vincent Delieuvin oversees the five Leonardo masterpieces
cues.en: NARRATOR: Vincent Delieuvin oversees the five Leonardo masterpieces
cues.zh: 旁白：文森特德利文 (Vincent Delieuvin) 監督達文西的五部傑作

cues.text: that hang at the Louvre.
cues.en: that hang at the Louvre.
cues.zh: 掛在羅浮宮。

cues.text: ♪ That's the largest collection in the world.
cues.en: ♪ That's the largest collection in the world.
cues.zh: ♪ 這是世界上最大的收藏。

cues.text: While Leonardo may be the most famous painter of all time,
cues.en: While Leonardo may be the most famous painter of all time,
cues.zh: 雖然萊昂納多可能是有史以來最著名的畫家，

cues.text: he completed surprisingly few paintings.
cues.en: he completed surprisingly few paintings.
cues.zh: 他完成的畫作少得驚人。

cues.text: Leonardo was really someone experimental.
cues.en: Leonardo was really someone experimental.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多確實是個實驗者。

cues.text: He didn't want to paint a lot.
cues.en: He didn't want to paint a lot.
cues.zh: 他不想畫太多。

cues.text: He wanted to paint a perfect painting.
cues.en: He wanted to paint a perfect painting.
cues.zh: 他想畫出一幅完美的畫。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: So what did it take for Leonardo to make a perfect painting?
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: So what did it take for Leonardo to make a perfect painting?
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：那麼李奧納多需要什麼才能創作出一幅完美的畫作呢？

cues.text: The answer may be lying right under Delieuvin's feet.
cues.en: The answer may be lying right under Delieuvin's feet.
cues.zh: 答案可能就在德利文的腳下。

cues.text: For the upcoming exhibition, he is working with a team of scientists
cues.en: For the upcoming exhibition, he is working with a team of scientists
cues.zh: 對於即將舉行的展覽，他正在與科學家團隊合作

cues.text: housed downstairs from the Louvre, at the Center for Research and Restoration
cues.en: housed downstairs from the Louvre, at the Center for Research and Restoration
cues.zh: 位於羅浮宮樓下的研究與修復中心

cues.text: of Museums in France.
cues.en: of Museums in France.
cues.zh: 法國的博物館。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Thanks to a new kind of scientific investigation, we are really able to get inside the painting
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Thanks to a new kind of scientific investigation, we are really able to get inside the painting
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：由於一種新的科學研究，我們真正能夠進入畫作內部

cues.text: and to understand how Leonardo was working to perfect the painting
cues.en: and to understand how Leonardo was working to perfect the painting
cues.zh: 並瞭解李奧納多如何努力完善這幅畫

cues.text: for a long, long time-- during five, ten, 20 years.
cues.en: for a long, long time-- during five, ten, 20 years.
cues.zh: 很長很長一段時間──五年、十年、二十年。

cues.text: It's really something really specific to Leonardo.
cues.en: It's really something really specific to Leonardo.
cues.zh: 這確實是萊昂納多特有的東西。

cues.text: NARRATOR: They are peering deep inside Leonardo's masterpieces,
cues.en: NARRATOR: They are peering deep inside Leonardo's masterpieces,
cues.zh: 旁白：他們正在深入探究列奧納多的傑作，

cues.text: hoping to reveal the secrets of his technique
cues.en: hoping to reveal the secrets of his technique
cues.zh: 希望揭示他技術的秘密

cues.text: that our eyes cannot see.
cues.en: that our eyes cannot see.
cues.zh: 我們的眼睛看不見。

cues.text: BRUNO MOTTIN: The eye sees something that it believes to be two-dimensional,
cues.en: BRUNO MOTTIN: The eye sees something that it believes to be two-dimensional,
cues.zh: BRUNO MOTTIN：眼睛看到它認為是二維的東西，

cues.text: but which is really three-dimensional, because there is depth in a painting.
cues.en: but which is really three-dimensional, because there is depth in a painting.
cues.zh: 但這確實是三維的，因為繪畫有深度。

cues.text: NARRATOR: For art historian Bruno Mottin, the first step is to understand
cues.en: NARRATOR: For art historian Bruno Mottin, the first step is to understand
cues.zh: 旁白：對藝術史學家布魯諾‧莫丁來說，第一步是理解

cues.text: the chemistry of Leonardo's paint, starting with the powdered minerals
cues.en: the chemistry of Leonardo's paint, starting with the powdered minerals
cues.zh: 萊昂納多顏料的化學成分，從礦物粉開始

cues.text: that were the source of his colors.
cues.en: that were the source of his colors.
cues.zh: 這就是他色彩的來源。

cues.text: MOTTIN: You have green, which is made with the scratching of copper plates,
cues.en: MOTTIN: You have green, which is made with the scratching of copper plates,
cues.zh: MOTTIN：你有綠色，它是用銅板刮痕製成的，

cues.text: you have vermillion, which is made with mercury, you have lead white, which is made with lead.
cues.en: you have vermillion, which is made with mercury, you have lead white, which is made with lead.
cues.zh: 你有朱紅色，它是由汞製成的，你有鉛白，它是由鉛製成的。

cues.text: But these can't be applied directly on a painting-- it has to be mixed with something else.
cues.en: But these can't be applied directly on a painting-- it has to be mixed with something else.
cues.zh: 但這些不能直接應用在繪畫上——它必須與其他東西混合。

cues.text: NARRATOR: These colored pigments are mixed with a liquid, like oil.
cues.en: NARRATOR: These colored pigments are mixed with a liquid, like oil.
cues.zh: 旁白：這些彩色顏料與液體（如油）混合。

cues.text: That gets painted on in layers.
cues.en: That gets painted on in layers.
cues.zh: 這是分層繪製的。

cues.text: ♪ In a cross-section of a painting,
cues.en: ♪ In a cross-section of a painting,
cues.zh: ♪ 在一幅畫的橫切面中，

cues.text: you have the base- which today is frequently canvas,
cues.en: you have the base- which today is frequently canvas,
cues.zh: 你有底座——今天通常是帆布，

cues.text: but in Leonardo's time, they used planks of wood.
cues.en: but in Leonardo's time, they used planks of wood.
cues.zh: 但在列奧納多時代，他們使用木板。

cues.text: On that is a coat of white that can reflect light.
cues.en: On that is a coat of white that can reflect light.
cues.zh: 上面有一層可以反射光線的白色塗層。

cues.text: As the artist works, semi-translucent paint is built up layer by layer
cues.en: As the artist works, semi-translucent paint is built up layer by layer
cues.zh: 隨著藝術家的創作，半透明的顏料一層一層堆積起來

cues.text: and then sealed with a coat of varnish.
cues.en: and then sealed with a coat of varnish.
cues.zh: 然後用一層清漆密封。

cues.text: In the end, our eyes see the interplay between the light reflected off different pigments
cues.en: In the end, our eyes see the interplay between the light reflected off different pigments
cues.zh: 最後，我們的眼睛看到不同顏料反射的光之間的相互作用

cues.text: suspended in the layers, creating depth and elusive subtleties.
cues.en: suspended in the layers, creating depth and elusive subtleties.
cues.zh: 懸浮在層層之中，創造出深度和難以捉摸的微妙之處。

cues.text: MOTTIN: Oil is a translucent medium, which gives to the mixture a deepness.
cues.en: MOTTIN: Oil is a translucent medium, which gives to the mixture a deepness.
cues.zh: MOTTIN：油是一種半透明介質，賦予混合物深度。

cues.text: You can see through all the layers.
cues.en: You can see through all the layers.
cues.zh: 你可以看透所有的層。

cues.text: You don't only see a flat surface.
cues.en: You don't only see a flat surface.
cues.zh: 您看到的不僅僅是平坦的表面。

cues.text: You have the feeling of what is beneath the painting.
cues.en: You have the feeling of what is beneath the painting.
cues.zh: 你可以感覺到畫作底下的東西。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo worked on the "Mona Lisa" for about 16 years.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo worked on the "Mona Lisa" for about 16 years.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多為《蒙娜麗莎》工作了大約 16 年。

cues.text: Can these investigative techniques help reveal, ultimately, what he was doing all that time?
cues.en: Can these investigative techniques help reveal, ultimately, what he was doing all that time?

cues.text: But now, experts aren't so sure.
cues.en: But now, experts aren't so sure.

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: For centuries, that painting was attributed to Leonardo.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: For centuries, that painting was attributed to Leonardo.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：幾個世紀以來，這幅畫被認為是李奧納多的作品。

cues.text: But during the 20th century, some historians said, "Well, it looks like difference
cues.en: But during the 20th century, some historians said, "Well, it looks like difference
cues.zh: 但在 20 世紀，一些歷史學家說：「嗯，這看起來像是差異

cues.text: compared to the other paintings." NARRATOR: Cinzia Pasquali has been brought in
cues.en: compared to the other paintings." NARRATOR: Cinzia Pasquali has been brought in
cues.zh: 與其他畫作相比。 」旁白：Cinzia Pasquali 已被帶入

cues.text: to restore the painting.
cues.en: to restore the painting.
cues.zh: 來恢復這幅畫。

cues.text: Can Leonardo's unique scientific techniques provide the clue she needs to finally solve the mystery:
cues.en: Can Leonardo's unique scientific techniques provide the clue she needs to finally solve the mystery:
cues.zh: 萊昂納多獨特的科學技術能否提供她最終解開謎團所需的線索：

cues.text: did Leonardo in fact paint this?
cues.en: did Leonardo in fact paint this?
cues.zh: 這真的是李奧納多畫的嗎？

cues.text: PASQUALI: NARRATOR: Restoration work is not for the faint of heart.
cues.en: PASQUALI: NARRATOR: Restoration work is not for the faint of heart.
cues.zh: 帕斯誇裡：旁白：修復工作不適合膽小的人。

cues.text: This painting may be in bad shape, but Pasquali is still taking her scalpel
cues.en: This painting may be in bad shape, but Pasquali is still taking her scalpel
cues.zh: 這幅畫的形狀可能很糟糕，但帕斯卡利仍然拿著她的手術刀

cues.text: to an irreplaceable masterpiece.
cues.en: to an irreplaceable masterpiece.
cues.zh: 成為無可取代的傑作。

cues.text: She scrapes away the yellow darkened varnish, revealing a vibrant color beneath.
cues.en: She scrapes away the yellow darkened varnish, revealing a vibrant color beneath.
cues.zh: 她刮掉黃色深色清漆，露出底下鮮豔的顏色。

cues.text: NARRATOR: But other parts of the painting appear more damaged.
cues.en: NARRATOR: But other parts of the painting appear more damaged.
cues.zh: 旁白：但是畫作的其他部分似乎受到了更多損壞。

cues.text: So Pasquali must rely on her training not only in art history,
cues.en: So Pasquali must rely on her training not only in art history,
cues.zh: 所以帕斯誇裡不僅要依靠她在藝術史的訓練，

cues.text: but also chemistry.
cues.en: but also chemistry.
cues.zh: 還有化學。

cues.text: ♪ The colors of pigment in paint can change or fade over time.
cues.en: ♪ The colors of pigment in paint can change or fade over time.
cues.zh: ♪ 油漆中顏料的顏色會隨著時間的推移而改變或褪色。

cues.text: But the chemistry of the pigments themselves can still be detected.
cues.en: But the chemistry of the pigments themselves can still be detected.
cues.zh: 但顏料本身的化學性質仍然可以被檢測到。

cues.text: Pasquali orders a special scan for the element copper,
cues.en: Pasquali orders a special scan for the element copper,
cues.zh: 帕斯誇利下令對銅元素進行特殊掃描，

cues.text: often used in green paint.
cues.en: often used in green paint.
cues.zh: 常用於綠色塗料。

cues.text: The scan reveals this dark area of the painting
cues.en: The scan reveals this dark area of the painting
cues.zh: 掃描顯示了畫作的這個黑暗區域

cues.text: was once a lush garden, until the copper in the paint darkened.
cues.en: was once a lush garden, until the copper in the paint darkened.
cues.zh: 曾經是一座鬱鬱蔥蔥的花園，直到油漆中的銅色變暗。

cues.text: PASQUALI: So we can see a lot of vegetable and leaves and plants and flower,
cues.en: PASQUALI: So we can see a lot of vegetable and leaves and plants and flower,
cues.zh: 帕斯誇裡：所以我們可以看到很多蔬菜、葉子、植物和花朵，

cues.text: and when you look on the surface of the work, they are not.
cues.en: and when you look on the surface of the work, they are not.
cues.zh: 當你看作品的表面時，你會發現它們並非如此。

cues.text: NARRATOR: While the beauty of these plants may suggest Leonardo's meticulous attention to detail,
cues.en: NARRATOR: While the beauty of these plants may suggest Leonardo's meticulous attention to detail,
cues.zh: 旁白：雖然這些植物的美麗可能顯示了李奧納多對細節的一絲不苟，

cues.text: that's not enough to say for sure he painted it himself.
cues.en: that's not enough to say for sure he painted it himself.
cues.zh: 這還不足以肯定地說這是他自己畫的。

cues.text: So the investigation turns to his brushwork.
cues.en: So the investigation turns to his brushwork.
cues.zh: 於是調查轉向他的筆觸。

cues.text: One of the most characteristic fingerprints of a Leonardo are remarkably thin layers of paint,
cues.en: One of the most characteristic fingerprints of a Leonardo are remarkably thin layers of paint,
cues.zh: 達文西最具特色的指紋之一是非常薄的油漆層，

cues.text: which can only be seen with a powerful microscope.
cues.en: which can only be seen with a powerful microscope.
cues.zh: 使用高倍顯微鏡才能看到。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Some Leonardos have been found to have as many as 30 layers of paint--
cues.en: NARRATOR: Some Leonardos have been found to have as many as 30 layers of paint--
cues.zh: 旁白：一些列奧納多被發現有多達 30 層油漆——

cues.text: many more than most painters.
cues.en: many more than most painters.
cues.zh: 比大多數畫家多得多。

cues.text: As she continues her restoration, Pasquali is looking for evidence of this unusual technique.
cues.en: As she continues her restoration, Pasquali is looking for evidence of this unusual technique.
cues.zh: 在繼續修復過程中，帕斯誇裡正在尋找這種不尋常技術的證據。

cues.text: But what was Leonardo trying to achieve with all those thin layers?
cues.en: But what was Leonardo trying to achieve with all those thin layers?
cues.zh: 但李奧納多試圖用這些薄層來實現什麼目的呢？

cues.text: Just ask a living painter.
cues.en: Just ask a living painter.
cues.zh: 只要問問活著的畫家就知道了。

cues.text: FLORENT FARGES: Da Vinci was always looking for beauty.
cues.en: FLORENT FARGES: Da Vinci was always looking for beauty.
cues.zh: FLORENT FARGES：達文西一直在尋找美。

cues.text: He's not just painting or drawing a tree.
cues.en: He's not just painting or drawing a tree.
cues.zh: 他不只是在畫畫或畫一棵樹。

cues.text: He wants to paint the perfect expression of what a tree is.
cues.en: He wants to paint the perfect expression of what a tree is.
cues.zh: 他想完美地表達一棵樹的本質。

cues.text: This aspiration to beauty is, to me, very inspiring as an artist.
cues.en: This aspiration to beauty is, to me, very inspiring as an artist.
cues.zh: 對我來說，身為藝術家，這種對美的渴望非常鼓舞人心。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Florent Farges is a painter in Dijon, France.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Florent Farges is a painter in Dijon, France.
cues.zh: 旁白：弗洛倫特·法格斯是法國第戎的畫家。

cues.text: In the tradition of the Renaissance, Farges runs an artist's workshop,
cues.en: In the tradition of the Renaissance, Farges runs an artist's workshop,
cues.zh: 秉承文藝復興的傳統，法吉斯經營藝術家工作室，

cues.text: but with a twist.
cues.en: but with a twist.
cues.zh: 但有一個轉折。

cues.text: FARGES: Hello, everyone, and welcome to a new video.
cues.en: FARGES: Hello, everyone, and welcome to a new video.
cues.zh: FARGES：大家好，歡迎觀看新影片。

cues.text: NARRATOR: His is a virtual one.
cues.en: NARRATOR: His is a virtual one.
cues.zh: 旁白：他是虛擬的。

cues.text: FARGES: This one is going to guide you through the entire process of classical figure painting.
cues.en: FARGES: This one is going to guide you through the entire process of classical figure painting.
cues.zh: FARGES：這篇將引導你完成古典人物畫的整個過程。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Most Italian painters at the time mixed their pigments into an egg base,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Most Italian painters at the time mixed their pigments into an egg base,
cues.zh: 旁白：當時大多數義大利畫家都會將顏料混合到蛋底中，

cues.text: using real egg.
cues.en: using real egg.
cues.zh: 使用真正的雞蛋。

cues.text: But egg tempera doesn't allow as much light to pass through it,
cues.en: But egg tempera doesn't allow as much light to pass through it,
cues.zh: 但蛋彩畫不允許那麼多光線穿過，

cues.text: so there is less depth in the painting.
cues.en: so there is less depth in the painting.
cues.zh: 所以這幅畫的深度較少。

cues.text: Instead, Leonardo decided to use an oil, like linseed or walnut.
cues.en: Instead, Leonardo decided to use an oil, like linseed or walnut.
cues.zh: 相反，李奧納多決定使用亞麻仁油或核桃油。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo was using oil.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo was using oil.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：李奧納多使用的是石油。

cues.text: Because oil helps to reproduce in the best way
cues.en: Because oil helps to reproduce in the best way
cues.zh: 因為油有助於以最佳方式繁殖

cues.text: the transition between light and shadow.
cues.en: the transition between light and shadow.
cues.zh: 光與影之間的過渡。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Gradually, Farges' portrait comes to life.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Gradually, Farges' portrait comes to life.
cues.zh: 旁白：漸漸地，法吉斯的肖像變得栩栩如生。

cues.text: For the finishing touches, Farges demonstrates how oil paint
cues.en: For the finishing touches, Farges demonstrates how oil paint
cues.zh: 對於最後的潤色，法格斯示範如何使用油畫顏料

cues.text: can be applied very thinly to create a subtle shading of light
cues.en: can be applied very thinly to create a subtle shading of light
cues.zh: 可以非常薄地塗抹以產生微妙的光影效果

cues.text: falling across the human body.
cues.en: falling across the human body.
cues.zh: 落在人體。

cues.text: FARGES: If I want, I can come back later and put another layer on top of that,
cues.en: FARGES: If I want, I can come back later and put another layer on top of that,
cues.zh: FARGES：如果我願意，我可以稍後再回來，在上面再放一層，

cues.text: to make this transition very soft.
cues.en: to make this transition very soft.
cues.zh: 讓這種過渡非常柔和。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's techniques are still being taught today
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's techniques are still being taught today
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多的技術至今仍在教授

cues.text: in his hometown of Florence.
cues.en: in his hometown of Florence.
cues.zh: 在他的家鄉佛羅倫薩。

cues.text: To make their paintings come alive, artists strive to capture human flesh
cues.en: To make their paintings come alive, artists strive to capture human flesh
cues.zh: 為了讓畫作栩栩如生，藝術家們努力捕捉人肉

cues.text: and the way light reveals its shape.
cues.en: and the way light reveals its shape.
cues.zh: 以及光揭示其形狀的方式。

cues.text: CECIL: Leonardo speaks about the smoky transition of light to shade.
cues.en: CECIL: Leonardo speaks about the smoky transition of light to shade.
cues.zh: 塞西爾：李奧納多談到了光與影的煙霧過渡。

cues.text: That's how we perceive in nature.
cues.en: That's how we perceive in nature.
cues.zh: 這就是我們感知自然的方式。

cues.text: The problem often with photographic images we see is that there's so much detail,
cues.en: The problem often with photographic images we see is that there's so much detail,
cues.zh: 我們看到的攝影影像經常出現的問題是細節太多，

cues.text: we don't get the broader effect.
cues.en: we don't get the broader effect.
cues.zh: 我們沒有得到更廣泛的影響。

cues.text: We see life very much out of focus-- we glance.
cues.en: We see life very much out of focus-- we glance.
cues.zh: 我們對生活的看法非常模糊——我們只是掃一眼。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Other artists of the day, like Sandro Botticelli, painted figures with hard outlines.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Other artists of the day, like Sandro Botticelli, painted figures with hard outlines.
cues.zh: 旁白：當時其他的藝術家，如桑德羅·波提切利，都用硬朗的輪廓描繪人物。

cues.text: But Leonardo used his fine layers to create soft transitions, obscuring the lines.
cues.en: But Leonardo used his fine layers to create soft transitions, obscuring the lines.
cues.zh: 但萊昂納多利用他精細的圖層來創造柔和的過渡，模糊了線條。

cues.text: This is his signature look, called "sfumato," from the Italian "fumo," or smoke.
cues.en: This is his signature look, called "sfumato," from the Italian "fumo," or smoke.
cues.zh: 這是他的標誌性造型，稱為“sfumato”，源自義大利語“fumo”，即煙霧。

cues.text: Unquestionably, the most famous example of Leonardo's sfumato
cues.en: Unquestionably, the most famous example of Leonardo's sfumato
cues.zh: 毫無疑問，最著名的達文西暈染法例子

cues.text: is that enigmatic smile of the "Mona Lisa."
cues.en: is that enigmatic smile of the "Mona Lisa."
cues.zh: 就是「蒙娜麗莎」那神秘的微笑。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Just look at the mouth.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Just look at the mouth.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：只要看看嘴巴就知道了。

cues.text: Look at the eyes.
cues.en: Look at the eyes.
cues.zh: 看看眼睛。

cues.text: You can't see lines.
cues.en: You can't see lines.
cues.zh: 你看不到線條。

cues.text: You just see the movement of the light.
cues.en: You just see the movement of the light.
cues.zh: 你只看到光的移動。

cues.text: That's incredible, and there is no comparison with other artists at that time.
cues.en: That's incredible, and there is no comparison with other artists at that time.
cues.zh: 這太不可思議了，與當時的其他藝術家無法相比。

cues.text: KEMP: There's no edge there at all.
cues.en: KEMP: There's no edge there at all.
cues.zh: KEMP：根本沒有優勢。

cues.text: It's all very uncertain.
cues.en: It's all very uncertain.
cues.zh: 這一切都非常不確定。

cues.text: This plays a psychological role, of course, because she is present but somehow not tangible.
cues.en: This plays a psychological role, of course, because she is present but somehow not tangible.
cues.zh: 當然，這起到了心理作用，因為她雖然在場，但不知怎麼的卻是無形的。

cues.text: She is idealized.
cues.en: She is idealized.
cues.zh: 她是理想化的。

cues.text: NARRATOR: For Leonardo, sfumato captured in two dimensions
cues.en: NARRATOR: For Leonardo, sfumato captured in two dimensions
cues.zh: 旁白：對李奧納多來說，在二維中捕捉暈染法

cues.text: what he observed in the three-dimensional world.
cues.en: what he observed in the three-dimensional world.
cues.zh: 他在三維世界中觀察到的東西。

cues.text: But in order to get the skin just right, he had to go deeper--
cues.en: But in order to get the skin just right, he had to go deeper--
cues.zh: 但為了讓肌膚恰到好處，他必須深入──

cues.text: to the muscles and tendons below.
cues.en: to the muscles and tendons below.
cues.zh: 到下面的肌肉和肌腱。

cues.text: Hold it like that.
cues.en: Hold it like that.
cues.zh: 就這樣握著吧。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Trudy Van Houten has taught anatomy for 30 years.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Trudy Van Houten has taught anatomy for 30 years.
cues.zh: 旁白：Trudy Van Houten 教授解剖學已有 30 年。

cues.text: Perfect.
cues.en: Perfect.
cues.zh: 完美的。

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: Leonardo da Vinci constantly inspires me.
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: Leonardo da Vinci constantly inspires me.
cues.zh: VAN HOUTEN：達文西不斷地激勵我。

cues.text: NARRATOR: She says the science of anatomy is beautiful.
cues.en: NARRATOR: She says the science of anatomy is beautiful.
cues.zh: 旁白：她說解剖學是美麗的。

cues.text: SYLVAIN: Would you like me to cut that?
cues.en: SYLVAIN: Would you like me to cut that?
cues.zh: 西爾文：你想讓我把它剪掉嗎？

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: Yes, please.
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: Yes, please.
cues.zh: 範·豪頓： 好的，請講。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Though the process often is not.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Though the process often is not.
cues.zh: 旁白：雖然這個過程常常不是這樣。

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: Nice.
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: Nice.
cues.zh: 範豪頓： 很好。

cues.text: You've beautifully preserved that tiny little vessel.
cues.en: You've beautifully preserved that tiny little vessel.
cues.zh: 你把那個小小的容器儲存得很好。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo dissected 30 bodies.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo dissected 30 bodies.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多解剖了 30 具屍體。

cues.text: And with no refrigeration, it would have been especially unpleasant.
cues.en: And with no refrigeration, it would have been especially unpleasant.
cues.zh: 如果沒有冰箱，那就特別不愉快。

cues.text: The intestines would've been a particular problem because they contain a lot of bacteria.
cues.en: The intestines would've been a particular problem because they contain a lot of bacteria.
cues.zh: 腸道可能是一個特別的問題，因為它們含有大量細菌。

cues.text: And even after death, the intestines become inflated, and larger and larger.
cues.en: And even after death, the intestines become inflated, and larger and larger.
cues.zh: 即使在死後，腸子也會變得膨脹，而且越來越大。

cues.text: That's where things were going to go bad quickest, and smell the worst.
cues.en: That's where things were going to go bad quickest, and smell the worst.
cues.zh: 那是事情變壞最快、氣味最難聞的地方。

cues.text: It's a very messy business.
cues.en: It's a very messy business.
cues.zh: 這是一件非常混亂的事情。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Many of the drawings from Leonardo's messy dissections
cues.en: NARRATOR: Many of the drawings from Leonardo's messy dissections
cues.zh: 旁白：許多圖畫來自李奧納多凌亂的解剖

cues.text: today live on in the most refined of places: Windsor Castle,
cues.en: today live on in the most refined of places: Windsor Castle,
cues.zh: 今天生活在最精緻的地方：溫莎城堡，

cues.text: just outside of London.
cues.en: just outside of London.
cues.zh: 就在倫敦郊區。

cues.text: Steps away from where Prince Harry and Meghan Markle posed for their wedding photos,
cues.en: Steps away from where Prince Harry and Meghan Markle posed for their wedding photos,
cues.zh: 距離哈利王子和梅根馬克爾拍婚紗照的地方僅幾步之遙，

cues.text: more than 200 Leonardo drawings are secured in the Print Room.
cues.en: more than 200 Leonardo drawings are secured in the Print Room.
cues.zh: 印刷室儲存著 200 多幅列奧納多的畫作。

cues.text: Martin Clayton is the curator of those drawings.
cues.en: Martin Clayton is the curator of those drawings.
cues.zh: 馬丁·克萊頓是這些畫作的策展人。

cues.text: CLAYTON: He couldn't help himself making a beautiful drawing.
cues.en: CLAYTON: He couldn't help himself making a beautiful drawing.
cues.zh: 克萊頓：他情不自禁地畫出了一幅美麗的圖畫。

cues.text: But what most interested Leonardo was the structure, the machinery of the body.
cues.en: But what most interested Leonardo was the structure, the machinery of the body.
cues.zh: 但李奧納多最感興趣的是身體的結構和機械。

cues.text: And this particular drawing is one of the finest examples
cues.en: And this particular drawing is one of the finest examples
cues.zh: 這幅特別的圖畫是最好的例子之一

cues.text: of Leonardo trying to understand how the shoulder works purely in mechanical terms.
cues.en: of Leonardo trying to understand how the shoulder works purely in mechanical terms.
cues.zh: 列奧納多試圖純粹從機械角度理解肩膀是如何運作的。

cues.text: There's no mystery of the body.
cues.en: There's no mystery of the body.
cues.zh: 身體並沒有什麼神秘之處。

cues.text: The body is a machine that can be looked at and analyzed in purely objective terms.
cues.en: The body is a machine that can be looked at and analyzed in purely objective terms.

cues.zh: 我們能夠重新發現藍色的原始形式和品質。

cues.text: It's a wonderful blue.
cues.en: It's a wonderful blue.
cues.zh: 這是一種美妙的藍色。

cues.text: And see how the painter represent these cities
cues.en: And see how the painter represent these cities
cues.zh: 看看畫家如何表現這些城市

cues.text: with that effect of humidity, of what Leonardo called the atmospheric perspective.
cues.en: with that effect of humidity, of what Leonardo called the atmospheric perspective.
cues.zh: 濕度的影響，也就是李奧納多所說的大氣透視。

cues.text: NARRATOR: But Pasquali's investigation has also uncovered details
cues.en: NARRATOR: But Pasquali's investigation has also uncovered details
cues.zh: 旁白：但是帕斯誇裡的調查也發現了一些細節

cues.text: like the harsh shading in the face, that don't show
cues.en: like the harsh shading in the face, that don't show
cues.zh: 就像臉上不明顯的陰影一樣

cues.text: the characteristic sfumato fingerprint of Leonardo.
cues.en: the characteristic sfumato fingerprint of Leonardo.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多的特徵塗抹指紋。

cues.text: I can't see Leonardo's touch.
cues.en: I can't see Leonardo's touch.
cues.zh: 我看不到李奧納多的觸感。

cues.text: This is a little mechanical.
cues.en: This is a little mechanical.
cues.zh: 這有點機械化。

cues.text: This line for the shadow is so hard, you know.
cues.en: This line for the shadow is so hard, you know.
cues.zh: 你知道，這條陰影線太難了。

cues.text: Leonardo don't do this.
cues.en: Leonardo don't do this.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多不會這樣做。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Pasquali and the team at the Louvre have solved a centuries-old mystery.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Pasquali and the team at the Louvre have solved a centuries-old mystery.
cues.zh: 旁白：帕斯誇裡和羅浮宮的團隊解開了一個數百年之久的謎團。

cues.text: The "Bacchus" cannot be attributed to Leonardo.
cues.en: The "Bacchus" cannot be attributed to Leonardo.
cues.zh: 「酒神」不能歸咎於李奧納多。

cues.text: ♪ But that doesn't mean he wasn't involved.
cues.en: ♪ But that doesn't mean he wasn't involved.
cues.zh: ♪ 但這並不意味著他沒有參與其中。

cues.text: Very often, his apprentices are actually painting the pictures, so he would conceive the general design of the work,
cues.en: Very often, his apprentices are actually painting the pictures, so he would conceive the general design of the work,
cues.zh: 很多時候，他的徒弟其實是在畫畫，所以他會構思作品的整體設計，

cues.text: and then the manual execution would be delegated to members of his workshop.
cues.en: and then the manual execution would be delegated to members of his workshop.
cues.zh: 然後手動執行將被委託給他的工作室的成員。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: The restoration has succeeded in bringing much of the original beauty back to this painting.
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: The restoration has succeeded in bringing much of the original beauty back to this painting.
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：修復工作成功地使這幅畫恢復了大部分原有的美感。

cues.text: But it also raises an intriguing question: should the same thing be done to the "Mona Lisa"?
cues.en: But it also raises an intriguing question: should the same thing be done to the "Mona Lisa"?
cues.zh: 但這也提出了一個耐人尋味的問題：是否應該對《蒙娜麗莎》做同樣的事情？

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: You have to imagine that under that varnish, you could see a wonderful blue sky.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: You have to imagine that under that varnish, you could see a wonderful blue sky.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：你必須想像在清漆下，你可以看到美妙的藍天。

cues.text: Probably also the face or the hand are more pink,
cues.en: Probably also the face or the hand are more pink,
cues.zh: 可能臉或手也更粉紅，

cues.text: like natural skin.
cues.en: like natural skin.
cues.zh: 像天然皮膚一樣。

cues.text: ISAACSON: If we could just take that varnish off,
cues.en: ISAACSON: If we could just take that varnish off,
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：如果我們能把那層清漆去掉的話，

cues.text: we could see it the way Leonardo really did it.
cues.en: we could see it the way Leonardo really did it.
cues.zh: 我們可以按照列奧納多的實際做法來看待它。

cues.text: But I think French governments have fallen for less cause
cues.en: But I think French governments have fallen for less cause
cues.zh: 但我認為法國政府的失敗原因較少

cues.text: than trying to take the "Mona Lisa" out of circulation and clean it.
cues.en: than trying to take the "Mona Lisa" out of circulation and clean it.
cues.zh: 而不是試圖將《蒙娜麗莎》停止流通並對其進行清潔。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Perhaps there is another way.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Perhaps there is another way.
cues.zh: 旁白：也許還有另一種方法。

cues.text: Could she be given a digital makeover?
cues.en: Could she be given a digital makeover?
cues.zh: 可以給她數位化改造嗎？

cues.text: That is what Pascal Cotte is trying to do.
cues.en: That is what Pascal Cotte is trying to do.
cues.zh: 這就是帕斯卡·科特正在努力做的事情。

cues.text: He has analyzed the "Mona Lisa" with a remarkably powerful camera and lights,
cues.en: He has analyzed the "Mona Lisa" with a remarkably powerful camera and lights,
cues.zh: 他用非常強大的相機和燈光分析了《蒙娜麗莎》，

cues.text: which he demonstrates using a replica.
cues.en: which he demonstrates using a replica.
cues.zh: 他用複製品演示了這一點。

cues.text: COTTE: We make the measurements in the basement of the Louvre, inside the laboratory.
cues.en: COTTE: We make the measurements in the basement of the Louvre, inside the laboratory.
cues.zh: 科特：我們在羅浮宮地下室的實驗室內進行測量。

cues.text: It's very emotional, to have the painting in your hands
cues.en: It's very emotional, to have the painting in your hands
cues.zh: 手上拿著這幅畫，心情非常激動

cues.text: without the frame.
cues.en: without the frame.
cues.zh: 沒有框架。

cues.text: You can look at this painting under this very intense light,
cues.en: You can look at this painting under this very intense light,
cues.zh: 你可以在非常強烈的光線下看這幅畫，

cues.text: that reveal everything that you cannot see usually.
cues.en: that reveal everything that you cannot see usually.
cues.zh: 它揭示了你通常看不到的一切。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: Cotte's extremely detailed scan of the "Mona Lisa"
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: Cotte's extremely detailed scan of the "Mona Lisa"
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：科特對《蒙娜麗莎》極為詳細的掃描

cues.text: and his analysis of the optics and chemistry of paint
cues.en: and his analysis of the optics and chemistry of paint
cues.zh: 以及他對油漆的光學和化學的分析

cues.text: reveal how the colors may have changed over time.
cues.en: reveal how the colors may have changed over time.
cues.zh: 揭示顏色如何隨著時間的推移而變化。

cues.text: It's not just the varnish that yellows and darkens,
cues.en: It's not just the varnish that yellows and darkens,
cues.zh: 不只是清漆變黃、變暗，

cues.text: but the pigments and oil in the paint itself.
cues.en: but the pigments and oil in the paint itself.
cues.zh: 而是油漆本身的顏料和油。

cues.text: Cotte's challenge is to reverse-engineer the effects of that aging.
cues.en: Cotte's challenge is to reverse-engineer the effects of that aging.
cues.zh: 科特面臨的挑戰是對老化的影響進行逆向工程。

cues.text: KEMP: This is not just photoshopping it and messing around with the colors,
cues.en: KEMP: This is not just photoshopping it and messing around with the colors,
cues.zh: KEMP：這不僅僅是修圖和亂搞顏色，

cues.text: which you and I could do and get tolerable results,
cues.en: which you and I could do and get tolerable results,
cues.zh: 你和我可以做到並獲得可以接受的結果，

cues.text: but this is based on pigment analysis.
cues.en: but this is based on pigment analysis.
cues.zh: 但這是基於顏料分析。

cues.text: NARRATOR: First, Cotte determines how much the varnish has darkened, and with his computer, peels it away.
cues.en: NARRATOR: First, Cotte determines how much the varnish has darkened, and with his computer, peels it away.
cues.zh: 旁白：首先，科特確定清漆變黑的程度，然後用他的電腦將其剝離。

cues.text: Next, he identifies what the color of each pigment
cues.en: Next, he identifies what the color of each pigment
cues.zh: 接下來，他確定了每種顏料的顏色

cues.text: would have looked like 500 years ago, and recreates them to see the colors just as Leonardo did.
cues.en: would have looked like 500 years ago, and recreates them to see the colors just as Leonardo did.
cues.zh: 看起來就像 500 年前一樣，並重新建立它們以像列奧納多一樣看到顏色。

cues.text: COTTE: For example, we know that Leonardo make the sky with white lead and lapis lazuli.
cues.en: COTTE: For example, we know that Leonardo make the sky with white lead and lapis lazuli.
cues.zh: 科特：例如，我們知道達文西用白鉛和青金石製作了天空。

cues.text: So, we have software that remove the wrong colors
cues.en: So, we have software that remove the wrong colors
cues.zh: 所以，我們有可以刪除錯誤顏色的軟體

cues.text: to obtain the genuine color.
cues.en: to obtain the genuine color.
cues.zh: 以獲得真實的顏色。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Then, pixel by pixel, Cotte restores those colors.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Then, pixel by pixel, Cotte restores those colors.
cues.zh: 旁白：然後，科特逐個畫素地恢復這些顏色。

cues.text: Suddenly, a greenish sky becomes brilliantly blue, and a bit of flush comes back to Lisa's cheeks.
cues.en: Suddenly, a greenish sky becomes brilliantly blue, and a bit of flush comes back to Lisa's cheeks.
cues.zh: 突然，綠色的天空變成了耀眼的藍色，麗莎的臉頰上又出現了一點紅暈。

cues.text: Finally, as the French say: voilà.
cues.en: Finally, as the French say: voilà.
cues.zh: 最後，正如法國人所說：瞧。

cues.text: KEMP: Suddenly, she doesn't look like a submarine goddess.
cues.en: KEMP: Suddenly, she doesn't look like a submarine goddess.
cues.zh: 坎普：突然之間，她看起來不再像潛水艇女神了。

cues.text: She looks as if she's in the fresh air, which is just terrific.
cues.en: She looks as if she's in the fresh air, which is just terrific.
cues.zh: 她看起來就像是在新鮮空氣中，這真是太棒了。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Cotte's restoration has brought Lisa back to life,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Cotte's restoration has brought Lisa back to life,
cues.zh: 旁白：科特的康復讓麗莎復活了，

cues.text: at least digitally-- closer to the state that Leonardo saw her,
cues.en: at least digitally-- closer to the state that Leonardo saw her,
cues.zh: 至少在數字上——更接近萊昂納多看到她的狀態，

cues.text: allowing us all to see the painting's legendary beauty
cues.en: allowing us all to see the painting's legendary beauty
cues.zh: 讓我們大家一窺這幅畫的傳奇美

cues.text: and the science it took: the geometry and optics of perspective;
cues.en: and the science it took: the geometry and optics of perspective;
cues.zh: 以及它所需要的科學：幾何學和透視光學；

cues.text: the anatomy behind her face; and the sfumato soft lines,
cues.en: the anatomy behind her face; and the sfumato soft lines,
cues.zh: 她臉後面的解剖結構；以及暈染柔和的線條，

cues.text: capturing the mystery and movement of life.
cues.en: capturing the mystery and movement of life.
cues.zh: 捕捉生命的奧秘和運動。

cues.text: But even with all the modern insights, the "Mona Lisa" is vastly more
cues.en: But even with all the modern insights, the "Mona Lisa" is vastly more
cues.zh: 但即使有所有現代的見解，《蒙娜麗莎》也遠不止於此。

cues.text: than the sum of her scientific parts.
cues.en: than the sum of her scientific parts.
cues.zh: 比她的科學部分的總和還要多。

cues.text: Pinning down exactly why we are so drawn to her
cues.en: Pinning down exactly why we are so drawn to her
cues.zh: 明確為什麼我們如此被她吸引

cues.text: ultimately remains as elusive as her smile.
cues.en: ultimately remains as elusive as her smile.
cues.zh: 最終仍然像她的微笑一樣難以捉摸。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Three years before his death, Leonardo was invited to France
cues.en: NARRATOR: Three years before his death, Leonardo was invited to France
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多過世前三年，他受邀前往法國

cues.text: to live and work for the king.
cues.en: to live and work for the king.
cues.zh: 為國王生活和工作。

cues.text: He crossed the Alps by horse or mule,
cues.en: He crossed the Alps by horse or mule,
cues.zh: 他騎著馬或騾子翻越了阿爾卑斯山，

cues.text: carrying three paintings.
cues.en: carrying three paintings.
cues.zh: 帶著三幅畫。

cues.text: Those paintings, including the "Mona Lisa," now hang at the Louvre,
cues.en: Those paintings, including the "Mona Lisa," now hang at the Louvre,
cues.zh: 這些畫作，包括《蒙娜麗莎》，現在掛在羅浮宮，

cues.text: where the doors are about to open on the 500-year blockbuster Leonardo exhibition--
cues.en: where the doors are about to open on the 500-year blockbuster Leonardo exhibition--
cues.zh: 500 年來轟動一時的列奧納多展覽的大門即將開啟——

cues.text: a celebration of a genius who fused together the worlds of art and science.
cues.en: a celebration of a genius who fused together the worlds of art and science.
cues.zh: 慶祝一位將藝術與科學融合在一起的天才。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo is an Italian Renaissance painter, but his genius is universal, and it speaks to everybody.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo is an Italian Renaissance painter, but his genius is universal, and it speaks to everybody.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：李奧納多是一位義大利文藝復興時期的畫家，但他的天才是普遍的，對每個人來說都是如此。

cues.text: ♪ BORGO: Leonardo wanted you to forget that you're looking at pigments on a piece of wood.
cues.en: ♪ BORGO: Leonardo wanted you to forget that you're looking at pigments on a piece of wood.
cues.zh: ♪ 博爾戈：李奧納多希望你忘記你正在看一塊木頭上的顏料。

cues.text: The idea is that you're looking at a real living, breathing being.
cues.en: The idea is that you're looking at a real living, breathing being.
cues.zh: 這個想法是，你看到的是一個真實的、活生生的、會呼吸的生物。

cues.text: ♪ ISAACSON: The key to Leonardo da Vinci
cues.en: ♪ ISAACSON: The key to Leonardo da Vinci
cues.zh: ♪ 艾薩克森：達文西的鑰匙

cues.text: is that he doesn't make a distinction between the beauty of nature that he studies in his science
cues.en: is that he doesn't make a distinction between the beauty of nature that he studies in his science
cues.zh: 是他沒有區分他在科學中研究的自然之美

cues.text: and the beauty of his art.
cues.en: and the beauty of his art.
cues.zh: 和他的藝術之美。

cues.text: ♪ He could have spent more time just being a painter.
cues.en: ♪ He could have spent more time just being a painter.
cues.zh: ♪ 他本來可以花更多時間當畫家。

cues.text: But had he done that, he wouldn't have been Leonardo da Vinci,
cues.en: But had he done that, he wouldn't have been Leonardo da Vinci,
cues.zh: 但如果他這麼做了，他就不是李奧納多·達文西了，

cues.text: and he wouldn't have painted the "Mona Lisa." ♪
cues.en: and he wouldn't have painted the "Mona Lisa." ♪
cues.zh: 他也不會畫《蒙娜麗莎》。 ♪
